<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par111" />{{GHGmargin-letter|111|e}}
4. The imperfect consecutive sometimes has such a merely ''external'' connexion with an immediately preceding perfect, that in reality it represents an antithesis to it, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=31}} ''and'' (''yet'') ''my life is preserved''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=8}} ''and yet thou chargest me''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; similarly in dependence on noun-clauses, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=25 ff.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|f}}
'''2.''' The introduction of independent narratives, or of a new section of the narrative, by means of an {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}, likewise aims at a connexion, though again loose and external, with that which has been narrated previously. Such a connexion is especially often established by means of {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} (καὶ ἐγένετο) ''and it came to pass'', after which there then follows either (most commonly) an {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=3}}, 8, 8:6, 11:2, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, &c.), or {{GHGterm|Wāw}} with the perfect (separated from it), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, or even a perfect without {{GHGterm|Wāw}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=1|hidebook=1}}f., 40:1, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=21}}, &c.), or finally a noun-clause introduced by {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|g}}
Rem. 1. This loose connexion by means of {{GHGheb|text=ויהי}}<ref>Exhaustive statistics of the use of {{GHGheb|text=ויהי}} in its many and various connexions are given by König in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1899, p. 260 ff.</ref> is especially common, when the narrative or a new section of it begins with any expression of time, see above, ''b''; cf., in addition to the above-mentioned examples (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=1}} ''and it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham''), the similar cases in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=1}}. Elsewhere the statement of time is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} with an infinitive ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, 29 39:13, 15:18f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=25}}) or by an independent sentence with the perfect (equivalent to a pluperfect, cf. {{GHGpar|106|f}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, or by a temporal clause introduced by {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=when}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲשֶׁר|translate=when}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָז|translate=from the time that}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=5}}; or, finally, by a noun-clause (cf. {{GHGpar|116|u}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי הֵם קֹֽבְרִים אִישׁ|translate=and it came to pass, as they were}} (just) ''burying a man'' (prop. they burying), ''that''...; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=11}} (the apodosis in both these cases being introduced by {{GHGheb|text=וְהִנֵּה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=5}}, 26, 19:37 (={{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=38}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=2|hidebook=1}} a noun standing absolutely follows {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} (as the equivalent of a complete sentence; see below, ''h''), and then an {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} follows.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|h}}
2. Closely related to the cases noticed in ''g'' are those in which the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}, even without a preceding {{GHGheb|text=ויהי}}, introduces the apodosis either— (''a'') to whole sentences, or (''b'') to what are equivalent to whole sentences, especially to nouns standing absolutely. As in certain cases of the {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}} (see {{GHGpar|112|x}}), so the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} has here acquired a sort of independent force. Cf. for (''a'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=23}} ''because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord'', {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּמְאָֽסְךָ|translate=he hath rejected thee}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=4}}, where the causal clause precedes in the form of an infinitive with preposition), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=21}}; for (''b'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=וּפִֽילַגְשׁוֹ|translate=and}} (as to) ''his concubine''..., {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫לֶד|translate=she bare}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=36}}f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=41|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 21:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=20}}f., 12:17, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=25|hidebook=1}}<ref>Cf. the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, l. 5 (''Omri'') ''the king of Israel'', {{GHGheb|text=ויענו|translate=he oppressed Moab}}, &c.—The peculiar imperfect consecutive in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=27}} b (in the earlier editions explained as equivalent to an object-clause) arises rather from a pregnant brevity of expression: ''I have observed and'' have come to the conclusion, ''the Lord hath blessed me'', &c.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34}} read, with LXX, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} before {{GHGheb|text=כִּשְׁמֹעַ}}.</ref>—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=14}} the preceding noun, used absolutely, is even regarded as the object of the following imperfect consecutive, and is therefore introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}.<section end="par111" /><noinclude>
